newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, band rumours remain.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, band rumours remain.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate early trading on Friday, with rumours of a central bank intervention band widening keeping the local currency well bid.

One major local bank dealer said offshore operators were continuing dollar selling on speculation of a band widening, but strong local support limited the downside. "The dollar is well supported at the 2,430.5 level. Local operators are not really convinced of an imminent widening," he said.
The rupiah rose to 2,430.5 on Thursday on the rumours before settling at 2,431.0 when the daily fixing was unchanged.
One U.S. bank dealer said the speculation was still present in the market although it was less strong than Thursday.
"I'm not really convinced but sustained dollar unloading from offshore makes you nervous," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.25/30.75 at 0220 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.5/32.0.
Tomorrow was at 2,430.0/30.5. There is no trading in value today due to the U.S. Independence Day holiday.
Economists and treasurers were mixed over the reason for an immediate widening. Some sourced it to an indirect recommmendation from the World Bank for a band widening.
They said a wider band would allow Indonesia to be better prepared for possible external and internal shocks.
But others said pressure in the market was not really heavy and a widening would ultimately appreciate the rupiah which could be then affect exports.
The U.S. bank dealer said a band widening now would not be good timing in the wake of economic instability in Thailand.
"If you keep it as it is, operators will be cautious about launching an attack on the rupiah because they know a band widening would reverse the market trend," he said.
The dealer said this uncertainty should limit negative implications from turbulence elsewhere in the region.

Dealers said operators were also watching a possible announcement of a fresh deregulation package on Friday, but they said it would have little effect on the foreign exchange market because the package was aimed at the real sector.
They said liquidity in the money market was a bit volatile, with overnight money trading at 14.0 percent after falling to 12.0 percent from an early 16.5 percent.
Tom/next swap was at 0.35/0.38 points.
The U.S. bank dealer said the band widening issue was not really absorbed because the market was slightly biddish in the swap market while keeping some pressure on the spot rate.
He said swap points were trapped in a two-to-three point range in moderate trading.
One-month swaps were at 12.5/13.5, two at 26.5/28.0, three at 39.0/40.5 and six at 80.0/81.5 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,427/2,619 and the conversion band at 2,427/2,475 on Thursday.
